newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan PM names small cabinet after suspense.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan PM names small cabinet after suspense.

text.p: Pakistan's new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif named his first six cabinet ministers on Tuesday, more than three weeks after hisPakistan Muslim League won a general election and eight days after he was sworn in to run his troubled country.
The six, given the oath of office by President Farooq Leghari, included some PML heavyweights and close associates of Sharif, but their portfolios were not immediately announced.

Among them was PML secretary-general and former finance minister Sartaj Aziz, Sharif's close associates Nisar Ali Khan and Ishaq Dar, and Punjab province PML chief and former interior minister Shujaat Hussain.
Other ministers were former National Assembly (lower house) speaker Gohar Ayub Khan and former information minister Abida Hussain, the only woman in the new cabinet so far.
Aziz was tipped to get the finance ministry again and political sources said Shujaat might return to the interior ministry.

A little-known National Assembly deputy from Sindh, Asghar Ali Shah, was named minister of state, equivalent to a deputy minister, and PML information secretary Mushahid Hussain, who is not a parliamentarian, was appointed prime minister's adviser with the status of a cabinet minister.
Sharif will name more ministers later, but the cabinet size will be much smaller than previous ones, which sometimes contained more than 30 ministers, political sources said.

The long delay in naming the cabinet appeared to paralyse government business and provoked speculation about power struggles within the PML as party heavyweights jostled for slots in the slimmed-down ministerial team Sharif had promised.

"This sort of thing happens when you've got a top-heavy government with so many people aspiring to become ministers," said Awais Bangash, spokesman for the opposition Pakistan People's Party (PPP) of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto.
He recalled that Bhutto was sworn in with four key cabinet ministers when she took power in October 1993. Sharif took his oath of office on February 17.
Mohammad Ziauddin of the Karachi-based Dawn daily newspaper said Sharif, who has pledged to keep the cabinet small in line with an austerity drive, wanted to include fresh, young faces.
But he was finding it hard to balance this objective with the demands of his senior party colleagues, Ziauddin said.

Another problem, he argued, was the Council for Defence and National Security (CDNS), created last month by President Farooq Leghari as an advisory forum grouping top generals and the ministers of foreign affairs, finance, defence and interior.
"The CDNS is being considered a supra-cabinet and all Sharif's senior colleagues want to sit there," he said.

Most of Sharif's close colleagues such as Shujaat Hussain and Nisar Ali are from his home province of Punjab. Including them in the CDNS would give it a "totally Punjabi profile", given that President Leghari and Chief of Army Staff General Jehangir Karamat are also Punjabis.
Pakistan's smaller provinces of Sindh, North West Frontier and Balochistan have in the past resented what they see as the dominance of wealthy and populous Punjab.
